messages:
maria: Heads up — seeing a sharp slowdown in the multipane dashboard when heatmap + legend are both visible. Frameskip and long main-thread tasks. :eyes:
aj: repro steps? is this on canary or prod?
maria: Prod, started ~18:10 UTC. Happens when switching time range and the legend toggles. Network shows repeated chunk requests for the viz bundle. Screenshot: https://perf.reports/heatmap-frames.png
tim: We pushed telemetry-proxy + prefetch-policy change in yesterday's canary, and the canary rolled to 30% ~18:12. Could be related to extra sync telemetry in render path.
kevin: I pulled logs from kvcache and see eviction thrash around the same time:
```
kvcache: evict key=visual-heatmap-v2 size=48KB reason=cache_size
kvcache: miss key=visual-heatmap-v2
kvcache: fetch /chunks/visual-heatmap.js?v=59
kvcache: evict key=legend-renderer size=12KB reason=cache_size
```
maria: that matches the network waterfall — same chunk requested 3x before it resolves. Looks like dedupe didn't catch when chunks are invalidated.
sara: Canary might have introduced telemetry sampling that does synchronous work during render. I've seen that flip the main-thread before. If the telemetry sidecar causes a micro-block, it can also surface as duplicate chunk fetches (race).
aj: Can someone paste the chunk response headers? If no `ETag`/`Cache-Control` or the client hash mismatch, revalidation will re-download.
kevin: Headers from one of the failing responses:
```
GET /chunks/visual-heatmap.js?v=59 200
cache-control: no-cache
etag: "abc123"
content-length: 49203
```
kevin: `no-cache` + aggressive kvcache eviction explains revalidation + eviction cycles.
maria: Hypothesis: telemetry change increased main-thread latency causing in-flight script requests to lose the dedupe key -> client retries, server responds `no-cache`, kvcache evicts, repeat.
infra-bot: deploybot: canary roll 2026-03-19T18:12:00Z -> 30% traffic.
aj: Short-term mitigation: revert telemetry sampling change on canary or increase client-side chunk dedupe window + make chunk responses cacheable.
sara: Agreed. I can push a quick patch to debounce telemetry calls in the render path (5ms) and set `Cache-Control: public, max-age=60` for chunk assets behind CDN.
kevin: Also propose increasing kvcache size for the UI hostpool by 20% to reduce eviction thrash while we fix headers.
maria: Can we do both? Roll telemetry patch to canary and patch CDN headers, then monitor LCP / frame drops.
aj: I'll open a canary rollback/patch ticket and schedule a tiny canary (5%) with the telemetry debounce first. If that improves frames, we can then push cache header change.
kevin: Quick client-side fallback possible too: if a chunk fetch is in-flight, keep a promise registry keyed by module id to avoid refetch on render churn. Small patch: add `inflightChunks` map.
```
// pseudo
if (inflightChunks[id]) return await inflightChunks[id]
inflightChunks[id] = fetchChunk(id)
await inflightChunks[id]
```

maria: Nice. That would help until CDN headers roll out.
sara: I'll draft the debounce PR now. @aj can you handle canary rollout plan + metrics (LCP, main-thread tasks, chart render success rate)?
aj: On it — will post plan here in 10m and attach perf dashboards. :thumbsup:
maria: Thanks all. Priorities: (1) telemetry debounce canary, (2) client inflight dedupe patch, (3) CDN cache header change, (4) kvcache size bump if still needed.
kevin: logging note — let's add a short kvcache debug flag to collect eviction stack traces for one hour during canary to validate root cause.
infra-bot: alertbot: perf-alert triggered for multipane-heatmap LCP spike at 18:09 UTC (p95 up 420ms).
aj: I'll update the incident board if we see >10% regressions after the patch.
maria: Will follow up with traces. Thanks.
